newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia mulls 10.68 trln rph transport projects.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia mulls 10.68 trln rph transport projects.

text.p: Indonesia's transport minister, Haryanto Dhanutirto, said on Monday the government was studying 76 transport project proposals worth 10.68 trillion rupiah.

"There are currently 76 proposals for joint ventures between state-owned firms under the supervision of the Transport Ministry and privately owned companies to build transport projects worth 10.68 trillion rupiah," he told parliament.

He did not give details, but said several state firms under his supervision planned to build tranport facilities mainly on Java, Sumatra and Bali islands in cooperation with local and foreign privately-owned firms.
The private firms included PT Humpuss Terminal Petikemas, controlled by President Suharto's son Hutomo Mandalaputra, which planned to build and operate a container port in Jakarta.
Humpuss will work in cooperation with state-owned sea port operator PT Pelabuhan Indonesia II, he said.
Also, PT Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada, controlled by Suharto's daughter Siti Hardijanti Rukmana, plans to build and operate a passenger terminal at Adi Sumarno airport in central Java.
Persada will work in cooperation with the state-owned airport services firm, PT Angkasa Pura I.
Angkasa Pura I also plans to expand passenger terminal facilities at Ngurah Rai international airport on Bali in cooperation with British Airport Authority Pacific Ltd.

Dhanutirto also said that 17 firms under his ministry in 1995 had total revenues of 7.08 trillion rupiah and profits of 737.68 billion rupiah. He did not say if that was net or gross or give comparative figures.
Total revenues were likely to rise to 7.84 trillion rupiah in 1996 and profit to 826 billion rupiah, he said.
